rows.source: HSE workplace heat-stress guidance
rows.verified: Heat stress occurs when the body's mechanisms for controlling internal temperature begin to fail.

rows.source: HSE workplace heat-stress guidance
rows.verified: Air temperature, work rate, humidity and work clothing or protective equipment can all contribute to heat stress.

rows.source: HSE workplace heat-stress guidance
rows.verified: Symptoms can include poor concentration, muscle cramps, heat rash, severe thirst, fainting and heat exhaustion.

rows.source: HSE workplace heat-stress guidance
rows.verified: Heat stroke can involve hot dry skin, confusion, convulsions and loss of consciousness and can be fatal without early detection.

rows.source: HSE workplace heat-stress guidance
rows.verified: Risk assessment should consider work rate, climate, clothing or PPE and individual factors such as age and medical condition.

rows.source: HSE workplace heat-stress guidance
rows.verified: Controls include removing heat sources, changing processes, using fans or air conditioning and shielding radiant heat.

rows.source: HSE workplace heat-stress guidance
rows.verified: Exposure can be reduced by lowering work rate, using mechanical aids and limiting time in hot environments or scheduling work for cooler periods.

rows.source: HSE workplace heat-stress guidance
rows.verified: Workers need training on heat-stress risks, symptoms, safe practices and emergencies, and employers should allow acclimatisation and identify susceptible workers.

rows.source: HSE workplace heat-stress guidance
rows.verified: Heat-stress risk depends on environmental heat, humidity, air movement, metabolic workload, clothing, hydration, acclimatisation and individual medical susceptibility.

rows.source: HSE workplace heat-stress guidance
rows.verified: General heat-load assessment, symptoms, engineering controls, exposure limitation, training and acclimatisation guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards guidance
rows.verified: Employers have a legal duty to protect employees from work-related stress by assessing the risks and acting on the findings.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards guidance
rows.verified: HSE's Management Standards cover demands, control, support, relationships, role and change.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards guidance
rows.verified: The demands standard covers workload, work patterns and the work environment and expects demands to be adequate and achievable.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards guidance
rows.verified: The control standard includes employees having a say over work pace, skills use, breaks and work patterns where possible.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards guidance
rows.verified: The support standard includes access to policies, manager and colleague support, resources and regular constructive feedback.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards guidance
rows.verified: The relationships standard promotes positive behaviour, conflict prevention, fair treatment and systems for reporting unacceptable behaviour.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards guidance
rows.verified: The role standard requires clear, compatible responsibilities and systems for workers to raise uncertainty or conflict.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards guidance
rows.verified: Early action can reduce impact, and employers may need individual action plans and structured conversations for workers experiencing stress.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards guidance
rows.verified: Work-related stress risk depends on work design, workload, autonomy, support, relationships, role clarity, organisational change and individual circumstances.

rows.source: HSE work-related stress Management Standards guidance
rows.verified: General risk assessment and prevention across demands, control, support, relationships, role and change guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.
